newsitem.title: USA: Congress candidates raised $790 million - report.
newsitem.headline: Congress candidates raised $790 million - report.

text.p: Candidates for Congress in 1996 election campaigns raised a record $790 million and spent $765 million, the Federal Election Commission reported Monday.

The election commission said Republican Senate candidates raised $158 million and Republican House candidates raised $267 million compared to $126 million for Senate Democratic candidates and $233 million for Democratic House candidates.
The other $6 million was raised by independent candidates or candidates in other parties.
The report said 316 candidates ran for the Senate, including candidates who lost in primary elections, and 2,289 ran for the House of Representatives.
The $790 million raised for 1996 congressional campaigns was $50 million higher than the $740 million reported by candidates for Congress in 1994 elections.
